# E003 -- Origameo Digital Brand Guidelines

- **Industry:** Real Estate / Workplace Solutions
- **Year:** 2021
- **Pages Sampled:** 1-2, 6-7, 12-13
- **Total Pages:** 46
- **Document Type:** Brand Guidelines v6.0

## Brand Strategy
- Sub-brand of HB Reavis ("Origameo by HB Reavis")
- Brand personality defined through characteristics (section 1.1-1.2)
- Comprehensive guide covering identity, applications, and digital presence
- Structured in 4 sections: Who We Are, Visual Style, Examples/Application, Digital

## Logo
- Wordmark-based identity (not a symbol/icon logo)
- Full name: "Origameo by HB Reavis"; shortened: "Origameo"
- Name rules: capital "O" only in text; only the logo mark uses uppercase
- Prohibited forms: initials (OHBR), all lowercase, all uppercase
- Three usage modes: Coloured (preferred), White (on colored/dark backgrounds), Grey (on light backgrounds)
- White logo required on colored or gradient backgrounds
- Endorsement line ("by hbreavis") in grey (#686C6D)

## Applications
- PowerPoint presentations, letterhead, Word templates, business cards
- Digital: website, social media identity, social media posts, ads

## Tone of Voice
- Voice: warm, deep, calm authority with youthful, familiar, natural quality
- Writing style: smooth, precise, approachable, friendly
- Inspirational and subtly enthusiastic
- Informal: "we" instead of brand name, contractions preferred ("we're" over "we are")
- Conversational over official; human, person-to-person feel
- British English on international level; local languages in market communications
- Avoid colloquialisms and overly familiar language
- Storytelling approach to communicate ideas and achievements

## Outliers / Unique Elements
- Detailed naming conventions (proper noun treatment, prohibited abbreviations)
- Strong tone of voice section with specific writing rules -- unusually prescriptive for a 46-page guide
- Sub-brand architecture with endorsement line ("by HB Reavis") and co-branding rules (section 2.9)
- Version 6.0 indicates mature, iterated brand system

## Quality Score
4 / 5
- Well-structured 46-page guide covering brand strategy, visual identity, TOV, and digital applications
- Strong color specification with all format values; good tone of voice detail
- Missing detail on typography, photography, and graphic elements from sampling
- Clear sub-brand architecture and naming rules
